relevance_note: Japanese cohort of 31 bulbospinal-type and intermediate-form Alexander disease probands, each listed in Table 1 with GFAP mutation, sex, age at diagnosis, age at onset and initial symptom ("A total of 21 unique GFAP mutations were identified in the 31 patients").
method_note: Table 1 (31 rows; patients as rows) was transcribed by a short Python script and checked against the table by eye; every span was then checked verbatim against the paper. Labels: Table 1 has a 'No.' column of bare numbers, so rows are 'Table 1 #<n>' (superscript a dropped from the label), except patient 12 and Patient 13, whom the text names ('patient 12' in Results; 'Patient 13, E362G' in Supplementary materials S3/S4), so rule 1 applies to them. Table 1 rows 1-12 sit above a 'Bulbospinal type' section row; the heading for rows 1-12 did not survive conversion, so only rows 2, 4, 10 and 11 (footnote a: 'subsequently classified with the intermediate form') are labelled intermediate form; rows 1, 3, 5-9 and 12 are given the paper-level label 'AxD'. Rows 13-31 are 'Bulbospinal type' from the section row. Variants are printed as protein-level short forms without 'p.' (e.g. R79H); recorded in variant_original_string and protein_hgvs_as_stated; no cDNA or transcript printed. Zygosity 'heterozygous' comes from the named group statement 'Forty-two Japanese AxD patients of 40 families with heterozygous GFAP mutations', of whom the 31 are a subset. In silico predictions (PROVEAN 'Neutral'/'Deleterious', PolyPhen-2, SIFT, Mutation Assessor, CADD in Table S7) are computational predictions the authors call not definite, so they are not recorded as authors' pathogenicity classification. Phenotypes: only the 'Initial symptom' column gives per-person features; NA (rows 7 and 24) gives no row. Checklist mapping: Dysarthria, Dysphagia, Limb weakness, Incontinence (bladder or bowel dysfunction) and Dementia (cognitive decline) mapped; 'Gait disturbance', 'Weakness', 'Limb clumsiness', 'Blurred vision' and 'Mental retardation' left not reported on the checklist because they do not specifically match an item. Subtype definitions in the Introduction (e.g. medulla atrophy in bulbospinal type) were not used as person-level MRI evidence. Ref column cells span several lines in the Markdown (e.g. '^7,\n10,\n11'); copied verbatim into source_reference_in_review. Empty Ref cells (rows 3, 12, 19, 20, 24, 29) are not reported. Association-study variants in other genes (Tables 2, S1-S4) are group-level genotype counts with no per-person attribution, so no variant rows; the PIK3C2G rs2305220 discrepancy is in an unnamed 'one patient'. No stacked ' / ' cells assigned to people. No contradictions found.
